changes: Re-read 'śrīmatkarṇadevopādhyāya śrīvarddhamānamiśraviracita' as a single epithet compound: Vardhamāna is 'the upādhyāya (teacher) of the illustrious Karṇadeva'. The colophon does not say Karṇadeva was his father, so the son_of relation is removed.
Moved the title 'upādhyāya' from Karṇadeva to Vardhamāna.
Karṇadeva: role changed from relative_only to other (a king or patron the author taught; not the reigning king of this copy), confidence set to low.
Replaced the son_of relation with Karṇadeva pupil_of Vardhamāna (medium).
Purpose cleared: 'bhavānyai prītir astu' is a blessing, not a statement of why the copy was made. It is now recorded in notes.

notes: 'karṇadevopādhyāya' is most naturally read as an epithet of Vardhamāna ('teacher of Karṇadeva', probably a king). It could also be a separate name, but nothing in the colophon supports the first reading's 'son of'. The end of the colophon has only invocations (śāradāyai namaḥ; bhavānyai prītir astu) and a corrupt formula 'kṛtohaṃ yas teno bhūyāḥ'. The copy names no scribe, owner, date or place. The work's title is damaged ('.. vistare', i.e. Kātantravistara). This colophon ends the third pāda.
